title: Group Anagrams
prompt:
Given an array of strings, group the anagrams together. Return the groups in any order (and words within a group in any order).

**Example**: `["eat","tea","tan","ate","nat","bat"]` → `[["bat"],["nat","tan"],["ate","eat","tea"]]`.

This is the canonical-key idea from the pattern lesson plus the `computeIfAbsent` grouping idiom.
hints: All anagrams share the same canonical form: their letters sorted.
`char[] c = word.toCharArray(); Arrays.sort(c); String key = new String(c);`
`map.computeIfAbsent(key, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(word);` then return `new ArrayList<>(map.values())`.

solution.explanation: O(n · k log k) where k is max word length. The sorted word is a canonical key: equal exactly for anagrams. (Alternative O(n·k) key: a 26-count signature string.)
